I’m not able to directly request or retrieve live quotes from plumbers through this system, so I can’t actually contact providers or pull real prices for you.

I can, however, set you up so you can get good quotes quickly yourself. To do that, I’d suggest:

1) Collect the key details plumbers will ask for:
- Type of faucet: e.g., pull-down, pull-out, touchless, brand/model (or a photo).
- Whether the new faucet is a simple swap or changes anything (e.g., going from 2-handle to single-handle, adding a sprayer, adding a soap dispenser, etc.).
- Sink/countertop type: stainless, porcelain, granite/quartz, etc.
- Access: under-sink access clear? any quirks (like very tight cabinet, garbage disposal, water filter, etc.)?
- Location: your city/ZIP and whether it’s a house, condo, or apartment.
- Timing: when you’d like it done (flexible vs specific dates/times).

2) Use these channels to reach a few local plumbers:
- Google Maps / Apple Maps: search “plumber” or “kitchen faucet installation” near your address and shortlist 3–5 with good ratings and several reviews.
- Local directories or apps (Yelp, Thumbtack, TaskRabbit, Angi/HomeAdvisor, Nextdoor, neighborhood Facebook group) to find additional options and compare reviews.

3) Send them a clear quote request message. For example, you can copy-paste and fill this in:

“Hi, I’m looking to have a new kitchen faucet installed at [your neighborhood/ZIP].  
Details:  
- Existing faucet: [brief description; e.g., ‘standard single-handle faucet with separate sprayer’].  
- New faucet: [brand/model, or ‘standard single-handle pull-down faucet’].  
- Work needed: remove old faucet and install new one; shutoff valves are [older/newer/unknown], garbage disposal is [present/none].  
- Access: [normal / tight / under-cabinet water filter, etc.].  
- Property type: [house/condo/apartment].  
- Timing: I’m hoping for [a few possible days/times].  

Could you please provide:  
- An estimated total cost (labor + any fees),  
- Any additional charges I should expect, and  
- Your earliest available appointment windows?”

4) When you get responses:
- Compare not just price, but also:
  - Ratings and number of reviews
  - Whether they’re licensed/insured
  - Warranty on labor (e.g., 30/90 days, 1 year)
  - Earliest availability and arrival window

If you’d like, tell me:
- Your city/ZIP
- What faucet you bought (or plan to buy)
- Any quirks under your sink

and I’ll tailor a short message you can send to 3–5 plumbers, plus a checklist of what answers to look for in their quotes.</action>
